item: Every crash trace says what kind of thread aborted (python / non-python / not-in-dump / no-trace / withheld)
summary: crashing_thread_kind is derived from the first faulthandler block: a Current thread label means a Python thread (the 10-14 lxml abort), thread blocks without one mean a thread Python did not create (inferred from how faulthandler labels), no block means an uncaught exception or empty dump; a session with no trace carries no-trace beside its reason. Found classifying the 10 SIGABRTs of the three sets: 3 traces opened with a plain Thread block. About 40 bytes per trace, at most 11 per report.
